1 Introduction 
1.1 Description 
TP6804 is an LCD controller supporting video scaling and up to two different resolution video source operations. 
It supports both MIPI-CSI-2 or up to 2 digital video inputs. Its outputs include one TTL (RGB 18-bit) or single 
LVDS channel, and one BT.656/1120 stream. After scaling, the output video can be either a video with multiple 
OSD overlays after scaling. The primary application is for Advanced HD E-Mirror applications up to FHD 
resolutions. 
 
1.2 Features 
• 
Supports digital video input formats: YUV / BT.1120 / BT.656 / BT.601 
• 
Supports MIPI CSI-2 video input with the Virtual Channel. 
• 
Support multi-layers font based OSD and SPI Graphic OSD 
• 
Built-in MCU with 4KB 2-way cache, I2C Slave/Maste

lti-layers font based OSD and SPI Graphic OSD 
• 
Built-in MCU with 4KB 2-way cache, I2C Slave/Master/Boot, Fast UART Configuring interface 
Input 
• 
Support up to 2 Digital video inputs including these formats: BT.656 / BT.601 or 
BT.1120 
 Supports programmable channel ID in multiplexed channel input 
• 
4-lane MIPI-CSI2 receiver support with data rate up to 1.5Gbps per lane(target) 
 Support up to 4 virtual channel data streams 
 Support both YUV422 8-bit formats 
Signal Processing 
• 
Support input video cropping, timing detection, and freeze detection 
• 
Brightness, contrast, saturation, hue, BLE/WLE, histogram tracking and DLTi/DCTi enhancement 
• 
Four front-end and one back-end H/V independent scaling machines with line buffers 
• 
Built-in 2D De-Interlace Scaling and Horizont

• 
Support Horizontal-Flip option for e-Mirror video path 
• 
Programmable Color Space Convert, R/G/B Gamma Table, Dithering and rich built-in pattern generator 
Output 
• 
Supports single-channel LVDS panel(s) or 1-channel RGB666 type TTL panel 
• 
ITU-R BT.656 8-bit outputs for any four channels or screen combinations

4.2 Scaling Machine 
The TP6804 has two built-in independent up/down scalers capable of Horizontal/Vertical independent 
scaling, with scaling factor from 0.125 to 8 times. It supports 2D De-Interlace scaling. 
 
4.3 Pixel Enhancement 
The TP6804 supports the typical Brightness, Contrast, Saturation, Hue, BLE/WLE, Histogram tracking 
and DLTi/DCTi enhancement. 
4.4 Image Control 
The TP6804 supports programmable Color Space Conversion, R/G/B Gamma Table, Dithering and rich 
built-in pattern generation.

4.7.1 I2C Slave 
The TP6804 supports 2-WIRE serial interface that is compatible to standard I2C protocol. Its slave logic 
always monitors the activities on SCL/SDA pair, supported bit rate up to 3.4Mbits/s. The TP6804 has two 
major register files, the scaler portion has default I2C slave ID as the following table: 
The above ScalerID register is located at P0_F1h, i.e., I2C master sends SlaveID matches the 5 msb 
bits, then TP6804 will acknowledge as the target. The P0 (in the mentioned P0_F1h) means the 
Page[1:0]=00, binary, available page number is 0~3), and the F1h means the I2C 2nd byte, command, 
will be used as the register index address. 
And the other major register file is in Memory Controller, its Slave ID is programmable at P0_F3

Once the MC_I2C_En set to 1, then TP6804 will also acknowledge I2C access when slave ID matches 
the P0_F3h programmable MC_SlaveID[6:0] above, and those registers in Memory Controller are 
accessible. 
4.7.2 I2C Boot 
The TP6804 also supports a minimum self-configuring mechanism: I2C Boot from external EEPROM. 
Once the reset trap of Boot_Sel[1:0] as 01b, then the I2C Boot handler in TP6804 will trigger internal I2C 
master to read the data (codes) stored in external EEPROM, and interpret those machine codes to 
instruction/data, then execute registers' configuring and some jump/loop/pause. The default I2C speed 
is 100KHz and can be programmed to

rs' configuring and some jump/loop/pause. The default I2C speed 
is 100KHz and can be programmed to support up to 3.4Mbits/S, also a High-Speed prefix code will be 
issue (option) to notice all the slaves hooked on the I2C bus. 
The I2C master in TP6804 is arbitration-capable (co-work with other I2C masters on the same I2C bus) 
and allows I2C slave to stretch SCL low when not ready. 
 
4.7.3 Uart_Cfg (RS232) 
The TP6804 has a proprietary RS232 protocol to supports fast RS232 access from external UART 
master (or USB to UART bridge), easily controlled from PC/NB. Follow those protocol, TP6804 can auto 
tracking the BAUD rate (allow dynamic changed, up to 1687500), and optional burst transfer to/from for 
quick communication.

The MI2C (I2C Master) block is triggered to perform I2C cycle(s) in two modes: one is PIO mode, like whenever 
the P0_DCh register is written will trigger I2C Master block to issue a cycle which is pre-
configured in P0_D8h~P0_DBh, at the same time those transfer type/counts also being set for 
MI2C to follow. The other is I2C Boot mode, when reset trap set to enable I2C Boot, this MI2C 
will automatically issue burst read from external I2C EEPROM and execute its instructions 
(propriety).

The 256 bytes burst write/read buffer of MI2C also shared with Talk mechanism, which acts as the communication 
buffers between external MCU (through I2C) and internal MCU.

[7:0], MI2C_Data [7:0]} - The first to the third bytes to be written after MI2C_SlaveID phase.

igure sequence from EEPROM with MI2C when read got 1.

Idx_StopAutoInc, OSD_Idx_PointerPort [6:0], OSD_Idx_DataPort [7:0] - OSD's configuration space is too 
big, so some portions (not frequently changed settings) are put into indirect space (Idx), which 
can be accessed from theses OSD pointer/Data ports. By default, the Inx pointer will auto 
increase after each read or write access to OSD_Idx_DataPort. These Ports are WO/RO. 
When read, gets current Idx pointer and the register setting of addressed by current Idx pointer 
Char_BlinkMode [3:0] - Char foreground blinking's duration and duty selection. Zero for blinking disabled. 
OSD_En- Turn off all OSD components when set to 0.

{OSD_Original_X, OSD_Original_Y}- OSD’s global coordinate. All components starting location are reference

MaskLt, MaskRt - Used to mask the left or right OSD portion outside display area, when horizontal wrap.

they can be manipulated as read-modify-write operation for special OSD rendering.
